product.olivetti-pcs286s16.summary: Documented commercial 16 MHz model, but not bootable in BluMach because no verified BIOS is currently available.
product.olivetti-pcs286s16.history: A 1991 Olivetti brochure documents a zero-wait-state 16 MHz 80286, 1 MB standard RAM, up to 8 MB on the system board, 16 MB in the system and 40, 80 or 120 MB disks. It possibly used the same TI/OLIMCU16 board that BluMach already emulates: a surviving unit shows the same TI TACT82300 family with EPROMs labelled "PCS286S REL. 1.06". That BIOS has not been dumped, so it is unknown whether it matches the known 2.06 or is a different version. The PCS 286/S sheet can create that board at 16 MHz as an experimental option.
product.olivetti-pcs286s16.warning: NOT BOOTABLE: no verified BIOS is available for the commercial 16 MHz PCS 286S. BIOS 1.42 belongs to the ordinary PCS 286 and 2.06 to the TI/OLIMCU16 board, which this model possibly also used; until its BIOS is dumped, neither should be presented as confirmed firmware.
product.olivetti-pcs286s16.technical.oli: Collection entry with photographs of a PCS 286S: TI TACT82300 board, Paradise PVGA1A video and EPROMs labelled "PCS286S REL. 1.06".
